text.p: Mining house RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd said on Thursday that calendar 1996 net profit by its Australian-based iron ore division Hamersley Iron fell by 12 percent to US$215 million from US$253 million in 1995.
Sales rose slightly to US$945 million from US$943 million in 1995, the company said.

"Although Hamersley Iron in Australia set production records in 1996 in order to rebuild stocks, shipments were six percent lower than the 1995 level. Profits, therefore, fell despite a modest price increase for deliveries in 1996/97," it said.
The mining house said iron ore production rose nine percent to 55.0 million tonnes.

World demand for iron ore fell in 1996 due to lower steel output in Japan and Europe, but Hamersley increased shipments to China and boosted production at the Channar mine in Western Australia by 30 percent to 7.8 million tonnes, the company said.
"Iron ore prices agreed with Japanese steel mills for deliveries in 1997/98 resulted in an increase of 1.1 percent for fines whilst lump ore prices remain unchanged," it added
